Aachho.story: Started in 2018 by Rimjhim Hada with a range of hand-block suit sets, Aachho is now run by Rimjhim and her husband Anurag Singh Khangarot, who joined as co-founder and CEO. The brand is built on quality and fine craftsmanship for modern women.

AnarkaliSuit.in.story: An online boutique that makes its own gowns and dresses for women and girls. Its stated aim is style without giving up comfort.

Anokherang.story: A contemporary ethnic-wear label for women, with suits, lehengas, bridal wear and designer dupattas. It was founded by a woman who spent 16 years in IT before turning to fashion, and its motto is "Just Be Yourself".

Autumn Lane.story: Co-founded by Richa Baid Agarwal and Aditya Agarwal, Autumn Lane was dreamt up while the two were shopping for Richa's bridal trousseau. They wanted women's clothing that never forces a choice between comfort and style.

Aykaa.story: An ethnic-wear brand with festive and casual Indian clothing for women, blending tradition with current trends. It has been in the business for over six years and talks about ethically sourced fabrics.

Begum Pret.story: Begum makes timeless daily and occasion wear, with artisanal hand embroidery, hand appliqué and fabrics revived on handlooms. It works with village artisans on a fibre-to-fabric journey, and dupattas and sarees are central to its story.

Bunai.story: Bunai was founded in Jaipur in 2016 by Pari Choudhary, on the belief that every woman is already beautiful. It is now led by Ajay Gupta (CMD), Amita Gupta (Director) and Pari Choudhary (CEO), and sells across India.

Chhabra 555.story: Founded by Krishan Lal Chhabra, the company takes its name from the plot number where it began. It covers the full range of women's ethnic wear: sarees, suits, dupattas, lehengas and fabrics.

Cotton Culture.story: Making women's ethnic wear since 2010, Cotton Culture grew from a manufacturing business into a brand with stores across India. Its focus is comfortable, everyday ethnic wear in good fabrics.

Divena.story: Divena began in 2015 and makes premium ethnic wear for women, with a focus on fit. It works with more than ten printing units, many run by hereditary hand-block printers.

Ethenika.story: An Indian label for women's ethnic wear that brings together handmade bandhani, hand-block ajrakh, chikankari, festive chaniya cholis and ready-to-wear kurti sets. It sources from skilled craftspeople across India to keep these traditions alive.

Farida Gupta.story: Over three decades of hand-block prints and embroidery, founded by Farida Gupta, who fell in love with Delhi's crafts and markets after moving there from Mumbai as a student. Her aim is to make India's craft heritage affordable and accessible.

Gaia Coutures.story: Founded by NIFT graduate Archie Chopra, Gaia is named after the Greek goddess of the Earth. It curates timeless pieces from distinctive Indian labels for confident, comfort-seeking women.

Ganga Fashions.story: Ganga began more than 25 years ago with the idea of bringing beautiful fabrics to life. It makes traditional clothing with a clean, modern design language.

Gulabo Jaipur.story: Gulabo Jaipur's prints start with a teakwood block carved by hand. It is known for hand-block florals, gota and mirror work, and makes shararas, lehengas and gota-patti sets for weddings.

House of Jamoti.story: Founded by Shubham and Mansi and based in Jaipur, House of Jmoti draws on the city's centuries-old craftsmanship. It designs ensembles that carry India's cultural heritage in a style for today.

House of Kari.story: A homegrown label taking Indian embroidery such as chikankari and Kashmiri aari to a wider audience, plus its own print line, Printkari. It gives over 10,000 women artisans across India a platform for their craft.

Idaho-o.story: Idaho was set up by entrepreneur Lalit Khatri as a tribute to the women in our lives. It specialises in flared outfits designed to make women feel comfortable and confident.

Idalia.story: Started in early 2018 by three young friends, Idalia mixes traditional outfits with current trends. It is known for kurta sets and kurtas in a range of lengths, prints and colours.

Jaipur Handblock.story: Jaipur Hand Block specialises in traditional block printing, from hand-carved wooden blocks to eco-friendly dyes on quality fabrics. It pairs the heritage craft with contemporary designs.

Jaipur Kurti.story: A brand of Nandani Creation Ltd, Jaipur Kurti was established in Jaipur. It makes ethnic wear for women of all ages, in all sizes.

Janasya.story: Janasya, from the word for people, was started by entrepreneur Vinay Kanodia in 2015. It makes festive and daily wear for modern, confident women at accessible prices.

Kalmkari.story: Kalmkari.in is devoted to Kalamkari, the hand-painted and block-printed craft using natural dyes. It works directly with artisans in both main styles: Srikalahasti pen work and Machilipatnam block printing.

Kalpraag.story: Founded in 2022 by Mayank Jain, Kalpraag sets out to redefine men's ethnic wear through craftsmanship and modern silhouettes. It has flagship stores and celebrity fans.

Khamaj.story: Khamaj India is a clothing brand inspired by slow living. It values quality over quantity and designs for mindfulness, simplicity and sustainability.

Kisah.story: Kisah began as an online experiment in making Indian fashion feel rooted in culture yet surprising. It is known for bold colour and close-up craft, and has grown into a brand with stores in several cities.

Krami.founders: Darshana Bagadiya, Bhumika Bagadiya, Dhwanil Bagadiya
Krami.story: Krami India was started in 2018 by three siblings, Darshana, Bhumika and Dhwanil Bagadiya. They source fabrics from Jaipur's textile markets and across India for comfortable, well-made everyday clothing.

Label Kanupriya.story: Label Kanupriya celebrates style, individuality, femininity and power. It makes clothes for dressing up whenever you feel like it.

Label S4U.story: Label S4U makes festive ethnic wear in every size, for every occasion from roka to pheras, haldi to cocktail. It ships to more than 20 countries.

Lakshita.story: Named after the Sanskrit for "distinguished", Lakshita blends Indian tradition with a contemporary look for everyday moments. It began as a small venture and now has more than 90 stores and a community of over 2,000.

Libas.story: Libas, from Zivore Apparel Private Limited, designs for the free-spirited, independent Indian woman. Kurtas are its forte, alongside bottoms and dupattas to mix and match.

Mansi Nagdev.story: Mansi Nagdev started as a space to express, create and contribute. The label focuses on fashion that keeps its cultural richness intact.

Narayani Vastra.story: Narayani Vastra comes from the Sethi family's generations-long legacy in textiles and clothing, with Jeetender Sethi at its heart. It makes women's ethnic wear rooted in tradition and craftsmanship.

Noor Bahar.story: Noorbahar curates crafted kurta sets that celebrate the grace and artistry of Indian wear.

Okhai.story: Okhai takes its name from the Okhamandal region of Gujarat, where it began. It brings handcrafted collections from artisans across India, made with designers in a collaborative process.

Origani.story: Origani was started by three sisters, Tanu, Manisha and Richa. Each piece is made by hand by artisans in natural fabrics, with sustainability at the core.

Pastels and Pop.story: Sisters Akanksha and Aarti Chhabra started Pastels & Pop in July 2015 to bring Indian handicraft to South India. It is best known for handcrafted juttis.

Phaelora.story: Phaelora grew out of years of weaving, dyeing and finishing cloth. It designs ethnic and semi-ethnic wear in-house for the modern Indian woman.

Ranna Gill.story: Ranna Gill blends Indian elements with global trends in pieces that are intricate yet bold. Each design moves from sketch to toile before it is made.

Resha.story: Resha India was founded and is creatively directed by Alisha Khan, out of admiration for India's textile heritage. Its pieces start with artisans who carve wooden blocks by hand.

Ridhi Mehra.story: Delhi-based designer Ridhi Mehra, a NIFT Delhi graduate, launched her couture label in 2012. It is known for pre-draped sarees, handloom fabrics and fine embroidery with a modern, wearable feel.

Saadaa.story: SAADAA began in December 2020 in a 100 sq ft garage, starting with women's everyday cotton pants. Its community passed a lakh women in 2023 and added menswear in 2024.

Sanskritam.story: My Sanskritam is a Chandigarh brand of everyday cotton kurtas, kurta sets and co-ord sets, many hand-block printed, in sizes S to 6XL. It began online and is still a fully online business.

Sheetal Batra.story: Sheetal Batra is known for standout fabrics and traditional handcraft. Garments come with a Heritage and Trust certificate and a promise of repair and renewal for years to come.

Style Union.story: Style Union opened its first stores in Hyderabad and Bangalore in February 2022, with everyday fashion for women, men and kids. It now has more than 180 stores across India.

Subhvastra.story: Subhvastra is an online women's boutique offering style without giving up comfort.

Suta.story: Suta started in 2016 with two weavers. The name, made from its founders' names, also means "thread" in Bengali, and it now works with over 17,000 artisans and weavers across India.

Taroob.story: Taroob spent decades exporting artisanal pieces to the US and Europe before selling directly online. It focuses on reviving Kalamkari and Kashmiri embroidery on cashmere, wool, silk and linen.

The Far Store.story: The F.A.R. Store draws on India's folk art, tribal patterns and indigenous crafts for contemporary designs. It began as a creative experiment and works to support artisan communities.

The Fashion Station.story: Founded in 2014 by Saba and Syed in Greater Noida, The Fashion Station is an online destination for ethnic wear that sources from suppliers across India. It serves customers in India and worldwide.

The Gaima Label.story: The Gaima Label is the brainchild of founder Garima Batra Dhawan, and began in a small sunlit room on a terrace. It makes made-to-order, handcrafted everyday wear that puts comfort first.

The Indian Ethnic Co.story: Mother and daughter Hetal and Lekhinee Desai started The Indian Ethnic Co. in 2016 from a bedroom in Mumbai with ₹50,000. It began with ajrakh, bandhani and hand-block prints, and now works with nearly 1,000 artisans.

Tjori.story: Tjori is a made-in-India fashion and lifestyle brand built around "Everyday Ethnic". It brings age-old crafts and rich textiles into modern, everyday silhouettes.

Utsav Bazar.story: Utsav Bazar has a large team of trained professionals and craftswomen. Its label combines culture, festive feel and Indian tradition.

VNH Naidu Hall.story: Naidu Hall traces back to 1939 and its founder M G Naidu, who set out to empower Indian women through clothing. It grew into a family apparel chain loved across generations.

Vaayu.story: Vaayu is a Kolkata clothing brand making conscious everyday clothes. It works closely with craftspeople and weavers across India to keep old techniques alive.

Varanga.story: Founded in 2015 by Shrikant Chandak and Ragini Roy, Varanga is backed by Keshvi Fashions, which has made sarees for 35 years. It offers affordable premium ethnic wear for everyday life.

Weavekala.story: Weavekala connects Indian handloom weavers directly with customers, from Kutch ajrakh and Bengal tussar to Chanderi and Andhra Kalamkari. It aims to pass on the maximum benefit to the weavers.

Xavielle.story: Xavielle began in 1998 as a wholesale and retail shop in Surat and launched online in 2018. It specialises in sarees, lehengas, kurta sets and kurtis.

Zlaata.story: Founded in 2023, Zlaata blends Indian culture with modern Western silhouettes. It makes affordable, fashion-forward clothing aimed at helping women feel confident.
